author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell Brand sits down with Sean Stone who shares one of the most bizarre and deeply unsettling experiences of his life. While reading a book by the legendary occultist John Dee Sean decided to attempt an incantation designed to connect with another dimension and what happened next defies rational explanation. The phone call Sean received immediately after the ritual left him shaken and questioning everything he thought he knew about the boundary between the physical world and whatever lies beyond it. A conversation that will leave you genuinely unsettled long after it ends.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell Brand asks one of the most profound questions facing Britain today — who could actually save the UK from its current spiral of moral and political collapse? Russell explores what it would look like if history's most transformative figures were here today from St Bernadette and St Teresa to Mahatma Gandhi, Winston Churchill and Julian of Norwich and whether their wisdom, faith and courage could cut through the chaos gripping modern Britain. A deeply reflective conversation about leadership spirituality and what kind of people a nation in crisis truly needs.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell Brand reacts to Oprah Winfrey's response to Elliot Page's transition and unpacks why the default position of total acceptance and empathy, while understandable on the surface, is built on a deeply dangerous idea. Russell argues that the belief that whoever you choose to be is automatically good and right is not compassion but a fundamental rejection of godly truth and a worldview that places the self above all moral accountability. A thoughtful and honest conversation about identity faith and why unconditional affirmation of every human choice is not the same as genuine love or truth.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell Brand reacts to a viral clip of former WHO Director General Margaret Chan openly explaining how the World Health Organisation receives its funding revealing that private donors like Bill Gates and governments like Germany hold enormous financial influence over the organisation's priorities and decisions. Russell asks the question that nobody in mainstream media will touch — if the WHO's own leadership has admitted that powerful private interests fund and therefore shape global health policy why does the world continue to treat the WHO as a neutral and trustworthy authority? A conversation about who the WHO really works for and why that question has never mattered more.
